mutations.because: K3's per-effect equivalence proof: renaming fade-in's own case label to rise-in's leaves the switch with two "rise-in" labels (the first, unreachable-for-fade-in one now returning fade-in's opacity track) and none for "fade-in" at all, so textEffectTracks("fade-in", ...) falls through with no matching case and returns undefined instead of a Track[]. Caught by motion-tracks.test.ts's per-effect equivalence assertions for both fade-in (opacity now stuck at the identity 1, computed independently from the old easeOutCubic(clamp01(local / entranceFraction)) formula) and rise-in (dy now stuck at 0, since it receives fade-in's opacity-track body instead of its own dy-track body). Also caught, empirically, by the compositor's own drawn-output suites (NodeCanvasCompositor.text-effect.test.ts, NodeCanvasCompositor.motion-tracks.test.ts's K3 describe block) and by NodeCanvasCompositor.text-effect-goldens.test.ts (the K3-gap golden family added after a reviewer found no golden ever set prepared.textEffect): all three throw a TypeError, because drawStaticText/drawSequencedCopy spread textEffectTracks(...)'s return value directly and undefined is not iterable. Stated precisely, not implied: the text-effect-goldens suite FAILS under this mutation, but it fails via that crash before any hash is even computed -- it does not move a golden cell, it errors out. The three ORIGINAL byte-identity gate suites do not move either and are never reached at all: NodeCanvasCompositor.motion-goldens.test.ts (48 cells), CanvasFfmpegVideoCompositor.byte-golden.test.ts (the mp4 byte golden) and NodeCanvasCompositor.layer-order.test.ts (the HL3 raster suite) all stay green under this mutation -- none of the three sets prepared.textEffect at all. So for mutation (a), the domain equivalence test and the drawn-output suites (including the new golden suite's own crash) are what catches it -- no suite here proves it by a moved hash.

mutations.because: Mutation (b) from the K3 brief: dropping scale-in's entrance-window stop leaves a single-stop track, which resolveTracks's sampleStops holds at that one stop's value for every t >= 0 -- the effect never settles, staying scaled down at 1 - scaleAmplitude (0.88) forever instead of easing back to 1 by t = entranceFraction. Caught by motion-tracks.test.ts's per-effect equivalence assertions at t = entranceFraction and t = 1 (both now 0.88 instead of 1) and explicitly by the dedicated settled-pose assertions ("scale-in at local=... has settled to scale = 1"), which is exactly the property this mutation breaks. Also caught, empirically, by NodeCanvasCompositor.text-effect.test.ts's rest-pose byte-identity suite (the restT(ken-burns-out) poster's hash moves, and the mid-entrance scale assertion observes 0.88 where 0.985 -- easeOutCubic's mid-window value -- was expected) and by NodeCanvasCompositor.text-effect-goldens.test.ts, which IS a genuine hash mismatch here (unlike mutation (a)'s crash): exactly the four scale-in cells move (legacy/entrance, legacy/settled, timeline/entrance, timeline/settled), all landing on the SAME wrong hash per platform (the stuck-at-0.88 pose renders identically whether sampled inside or past the window), while all twelve other cells (fade-in/rise-in/slide-in x legacy/timeline x entrance/settled) stay exactly as committed on both darwin-arm64 and linux-x64. The three ORIGINAL byte-identity gate suites still do not move, for the same reason as mutation (a): NodeCanvasCompositor.motion-goldens.test.ts (48 cells), CanvasFfmpegVideoCompositor.byte-golden.test.ts (the mp4 byte golden) and NodeCanvasCompositor.layer-order.test.ts (the HL3 raster suite) never set prepared.textEffect, so the mutated branch is never reached by them.
